free_text: The patient is a 70-year-old male with a high PSA of 9.3 ng/mL and a biopsy-proven Gleason 4+3 adenocarcinoma (ISUP grade group 3). MRI shows a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone, with no evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Given the high-risk features and elevated PSA, the management assessment focuses on reviewing individual treatment benefit and preferences regarding active treatment options.
